{
  "candidate_rtl": "module crc32_d8 (
    input  wire [7:0]  data_in,
    input  wire [31:0] state_in,
    output wire [7:0]  data_out,
    output wire [31:0] state_out
);
    // Fold matching data and state bits before distributing the CRC terms.
    wire [7:0] q;
    assign q = data_in ^ state_in[7:0];

    // Feedback bits emitted by the eight reflected Galois steps.
    assign data_out[5:0] = q[5:0];
    assign data_out[6] = q[6] ^ q[0];
    assign data_out[7] = q[7] ^ q[1];

    // Constant coefficient matrix for eight reflected shifts.
    function [7:0] coefficient_mask;
        input integer output_bit;
        reg [31:0] v;
        integer k;
        integer step;
        begin
            coefficient_mask = 8'b0;
            for (k = 0; k < 8; k = k + 1) begin
                v = 32'h00000001 << k;
                for (step = 0; step < 8; step = step + 1) begin
                    if (v[0])
                        v = (v >> 1) ^ 32'hedb88320;
                    else
                        v = v >> 1;
                end
                coefficient_mask[k] = v[output_bit];
            end
        end
    endfunction

    function integer population;
        input [7:0] mask;
        integer k;
        begin
            population = 0;
            for (k = 0; k < 8; k = k + 1)
                population = population + mask[k];
        end
    endfunction

    function integer selected_index;
        input [7:0] mask;
        input integer ordinal;
        integer k;
        integer seen;
        begin
            selected_index = 0;
            seen = 0;
            for (k = 0; k < 8; k = k + 1) begin
                if (mask[k]) begin
                    if (seen == ordinal)
                        selected_index = k;
                    seen = seen + 1;
                end
            end
        end
    endfunction

    genvar b, j;
    generate
        for (b = 0; b < 32; b = b + 1) begin : output_bit
            localparam [7:0] MASK = coefficient_mask(b);
            localparam integer Q_COUNT = population(MASK);
            localparam integer COUNT = Q_COUNT + ((b < 24) ? 1 : 0);

            if (COUNT == 0) begin : empty
                assign state_out[b] = 1'b0;
            end else begin : parity
                // A compact binary heap gives a balanced XOR tree without
                // introducing a separate final XOR for the shifted state.
                wire [2*COUNT-1:1] tree;
                for (j = 0; j < COUNT; j = j + 1) begin : leaf
                    if (j < Q_COUNT) begin : feedback_term
                        localparam integer INDEX = selected_index(MASK, j);
                        assign tree[COUNT+j] = q[INDEX];
                    end else begin : shifted_term
                        if (b < 24) begin : present
                            assign tree[COUNT+j] = state_in[b+8];
                        end else begin : absent
                            assign tree[COUNT+j] = 1'b0;
                        end
                    end
                end
                for (j = 1; j < COUNT; j = j + 1) begin : branch
                    assign tree[j] = tree[2*j] ^ tree[2*j+1];
                end
                assign state_out[b] = tree[1];
            end
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The original expanded parity equations distribute state and data terms separately. Wide XOR cones and repeated input distribution can dominate mapped maximum data arrival. Factoring reduces the parity width, although the shared feedback signals can become fanout bottlenecks.",
  "rewrite": "Specialize the fixed reflected CRC32 byte transform. First compute q = data_in XOR state_in[7:0], then apply the constant eight-step reflected polynomial matrix using balanced binary XOR trees. Include each surviving upper-state bit as a tree leaf rather than adding a separate final XOR stage. Preserve data_out explicitly, including the feedback corrections on bits 6 and 7.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to improve arrival time through narrower, balanced parity cones and fewer duplicated XOR operations. The intended state-output structure has at most four two-input XOR levels from a low-state or data input before mapping. No mapped timing measurement, SAT proof, or electrical-check result is available here; improvement and acceptance require the specified evaluation flow.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Expected to reduce XOR count relative to independently expanded 40-input equations. Shared q signals require fanout buffering, which may offset some area and timing savings. Compliance with the 2752.64 um^2 cap and zero reported electrical violations has not been measured.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Combinational crc32_d8 with the exact requested port widths and directions. The transform uses reflected polynomial 0xEDB88320, equivalent to the supplied 0x04C11DB7 configuration, for exactly eight shifts with feed-forward disabled. All 40 input bits remain arbitrary and all 40 outputs are implemented. No initialization, framing, reset, inversion, gating, sequential state, or assumptions are introduced. Parameter settings outside this fixed instance are intentionally unsupported."
}
